name: Towers of Doom
theme: Capture Altars and hold Bell Towers to bombard the enemy Core, as direct Hero attacks cannot damage it.
firstObjective: Warning at 1:45, spawns at 2:15 (~1:30 cooldown after an Altar wave finishes)
spawnPattern: 3 fixed Altar locations (Top, Mid & Bottom); spawns single or simultaneous Altars across waves in a set rotation

mechanic.title: Bell Towers & Altar Bombardment
mechanic.description: Cores cannot be attacked directly—instead, channeling active Altars fires shots at the enemy Core. Each Bell Tower your team controls adds a bonus shot to your Altar salvo, and holding all 6 Bell Towers causes your Core to fire periodic extra shots at the enemy Core.

camps.name: Sapper Camps (2 Camps)
camps.notes: Located in the outer lanes. Pumpkin-throwing mercenaries that march down lanes and detonate directly against enemy Bell Towers if left unchecked.

camps.name: Gunner / Centurion Camp (2 Camps)
camps.notes: Ranged mercenaries that apply sustained pressure and attack Bell Towers from a distance.

camps.name: Headless Horseman Boss (1 Camp)
camps.notes: Located in the central lane. Capturing the Boss summons a pushing mercenary and fires 4 shots directly into the enemy Core.

strategy: Towers of Doom shifts value away from standard Core sieges toward Altar rotations, Bell Tower flips, and map-wide vision/mobility. Global Heroes (such as Falstad, Dehaka, or Brightwing) excel at answering split spawns, while holding or flipping Bell Towers and timing Sapper pushes right before Altar phases forces tough defensive choices.
notes: When a Bell Tower is captured, it also briefly disables nearby enemy defenses and flips ownership to the capturing team—use that window to push waves or secure vision, and watch the central Headless Horseman closely in the mid-to-late game since 4 direct Core shots can swing close Core races.
